news.originalContent:
KEREM YUCEL/AFP via Getty Images

Minneapolis City Council members voted Thursday to keep new data centers inside existing downtown buildings, and larger ones would have to buy renewable power.

The 7-6 vote sends the ordinance to Democratic Mayor Jacob Frey, KSTP reported. A new data center can use up to 50,000 square feet for servers, or up to 150,000 square feet if the operator signs up to buy renewable power for all of the electricity it uses, the ordinance shows.

“Democrats spent the election promising affordability and are already finding new ways to make their communities poorer,” American Energy Leadership Institute President Chris Johnson said in a statement to the Daily Caller News Foundation. “The AI boom represents an enormous opportunity to attract private investment, expand the tax base, and finance new power generation. Minneapolis Democrats seem determined to make sure somebody else gets all of that.”

Oakland’s City Council voted Tuesday to extend its own pause on new data centers until October 2027, the Oaklandside reported.

Some Minneapolis council members who back a ban saw the midterms as a vote on data centers, Fox 9 reported. Democrats who ran for governor in four states this fall said they wanted to pause new data centers. (RELATED: Texans Elect Democrat Governor Who Vowed To Freeze Data Center Construction)

The offices of Frey and Council Members Robin Wonsley and Aurin Chowdhury did not respond to requests for comment. Oakland Councilmember Carroll Fife and the Data Center Coalition, which represents the industry, also did not respond.

A new data center has to go into a building that was standing as of Jan. 1, 2027. That building needs at least one other main use, the committee version states. The servers cannot go on the first or second floor, and they have to be at least 100 feet from any home on a nearby property. Applications must also list expected water, electricity and generator use.

Council members pushing for a full ban, or for a council vote on every new data center, fell short on a 6-6 tie Monday, MPR News reported.

Yesterday, Council Members brought forward a ban on data centers in Minneapolis. We also fought to strengthen the ordinance, including an amendment to protect residents’ voices in deciding whether data centers belong in their communities. Both amendments failed by just ONE vote. pic.twitter.com/pt8RpAGECE

“We don’t need more computers in our downtown,” Council Member Soren Stevenson said, according to MPR News. “We need people down here, and so I want to fight for a vision where people are thriving in our city, not for a vision where stockholders are thriving in our city.”

Council Member Elizabeth Shaffer, who helped write the rules, said that the city’s construction workers are short on jobs.

“Do data centers drive a lot of permanent jobs? No. Do they drive more jobs than vacant space? Absolutely,” she said, according to MPR News.

All members of the Minneapolis City Council are Democrats, except for Wonsely who sits as an independent affiliated with the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA).

Frey would veto the package if it included the stricter amendments from the city’s planning commission, Council Member Linea Palmisano said Monday, according to MPR News. His office told the outlet before Thursday’s vote that he “supports the regulatory framework” of the compromise approved Monday.

The final version limits data centers to either of two overlay districts downtown, KSTP reported. The council will have to approve each new data center, Fox 9 reported.

Council Member Jamal Osman said city staff and colleagues told him Frey would veto an overlay district, according to MPR News. Council members said they were confident Frey would approve the ordinance, KARE 11 reported.

Council members added the approval requirement Thursday and plan to meet again Nov. 20 to take up a possible veto, MPR News reported.

The city’s current moratorium, which has paused most new data centers for six months, expires Nov. 21 and never applied to downtown projects smaller than 350,000 square feet, MPR News reported.

“Xcel Energy has served data centers in downtown Minneapolis and elsewhere on our distribution system for more than 15 years, although we are seeing increased interest today,” the utility said in a statement to the DCNF. “New loads on the grid, such as data centers, can actually put downward pressure on customer rates by spreading fixed system costs across a broader number of customers.”

“The City of Minneapolis is once again making a bad situation worse,” Darren Nelson, a policy fellow at the Minnesota-based Center of the American Experiment, said in a statement to the DCNF. “They are trying to force data centers into ‘empty office and commercial buildings,’ that their Woke policies created.”

Nelson also pointed to research from the Electric Power Research Institute. The group’s study estimated that growth in data centers lowered average residential power rates by about 6 percent from 2019 to 2024.

“People in the Twin Cities, and state of Minnesota, should be worried about affordability, but not because of data centers,” he said.

Oakland’s council approved the extension unanimously, the Oaklandside reported. Fife, who wrote it, said that the 10 months will give the city time to look at how data centers affect Oakland and come up with rules.

“We’re seeing an uprising across the country when it comes to how data centers are operating,” Fife said during the meeting.

Richmond and San Francisco have also paused new data centers, according to the outlet.

The city got about 1,600 written comments on the rules, and almost half of them asked for an outright ban, an MPR News analysis found.

news.title: ایتالیا شرکت متا را بابت دسترسی به عکس‌های کاربران  فیسبوک، بیش از ۸۰۰ میلیون یورو جریمه کرد
news.originalSummary:

news.originalContent:
ایتالیا، شرکت متا، غول شبکه‌های اجتماعی، را به‌دلیل دسترسی به عکس‌های کاربران اندروید بدون دریافت رضایت صریح آنها، ۸۰۵ میلیون یورو (معادل ۸۸۷ میلیون دلار) جریمه کرده‌ است.

سازمان حفاظت از داده‌های ایتالیا اعلام کرده است که متا به حدود ۲۰ میلیون کاربر تلفن‌های هوشمند اطلاع‌رسانی مناسبی نکرده بود که از طریق یکی از قابلیت‌های اپلیکیشن فیسبوک به عکس‌ها و ویدیوهایشان دسترسی دارد.

این نهاد به متا دو ماه مهلت داده است تا این قابلیت را به‌طور پیش‌فرض غیرفعال کند و برای استفاده از آن، رضایت جداگانه کاربران را بگیرد.

این یکی از بزرگترین جریمه‌هایی است که تاکنون یک نهاد ایتالیایی علیه یک شرکت بزرگ فناوری اعمال کرده است.

موضوع این جریمه به قابلیتی مربوط می‌شود که عکس‌ها و ویدیوهای موجود در گالری تلفن همراه کاربران را به‌عنوان پیشنهادهایی برای انتشار پست در فیسبوک نمایش می‌دهد.

فیسبوک برای دسترسی به گالری عکس کاربران، فقط یک مجوز کلی در سطح اپلیکیشن درخواست می‌کرد.

به گفته نهاد ناظر ایتالیایی، اطلاعیه‌ای که پیش از آن به کاربران نمایش داده می‌شد، به‌روشنی توضیح نمی‌داد که این مجوز به فیسبوک اجازه می‌دهد بر اساس عکس‌های موجود در گالری تلفن همراه آنها هم پیشنهادهایی ارائه کند.

این نهاد اعلام کرد که در تعیین میزان جریمه، «تعداد زیاد افراد متأثر از این موضوع» و این واقعیت را در نظر گرفته است که این وضعیت «همچنان برای کاربرانی که اپلیکیشن خود را به‌روزرسانی نکرده‌اند و همچنین کسانی که پیشتر با این سازوکار موافقت کرده‌اند، ادامه دارد.»

نهاد ناظر ایتالیایی همچنین به «عدم همکاری متا» اشاره کرد. بی‌بی‌سی برای دریافت توضیحات در این باره با متا تماس گرفته است.

متا که همچون فیسبوک، شرکت مادر اینستاگرام و واتس‌اپ است ماه گذشته به‌دلیل شیوه‌های تجاری خود با بزرگترین جریمه تاریخ این شرکت روبه‌رو شد.

پس از آن که مشخص شد متا سال‌ها درباره نحوه مدیریت اطلاعات کاربران فیسبوک به افکار عمومی دروغ گفته، یک قاضی در ایالت نیومکزیکوی آمریکا این شرکت را به پرداخت ۲۵ میلیارد دلار  محکوم کرد.

news.title: بازگشت ناوشکن آمریکایی پس از ۳۵۷ روز ماموریت و شلیک ده‌ها موشک به ایران
news.originalSummary:
منبع تصویر، AFP via Getty Images

ناوشکن آمریکایی «یو‌اس‌اس اسپروئنس» که در جریان جنگ آمریکا و اسرائیل علیه ایران ده‌ها موشک کروز تاماهاک شلیک کرده بود، پس از ۳۵۷ روز ماموریت به پایگاه خود در سن‌دیگو در ایالت کالیفرنیا بازگشت. به گفته نیروی دریایی آمریکا، این طولانی‌ترین ماموریت یک ناوشکن این کشور از زمان جنگ جهانی دوم بوده است.

news.originalContent:
منبع تصویر، AFP via Getty Images

ناوشکن آمریکایی «یو‌اس‌اس اسپروئنس» که در جریان جنگ آمریکا و اسرائیل علیه ایران ده‌ها موشک کروز تاماهاک شلیک کرده بود، پس از ۳۵۷ روز ماموریت به پایگاه خود در سن‌دیگو در ایالت کالیفرنیا بازگشت. به گفته نیروی دریایی آمریکا، این طولانی‌ترین ماموریت یک ناوشکن این کشور از زمان جنگ جهانی دوم بوده است.

نیروی دریایی آمریکا روز جمعه ۱۳ نوامبر اعلام کرد که ناوشکن اسپروئنس پس از نزدیک به یک سال حضور در ماموریت‌های دریایی و نظامی، به پایگاه خود بازگشته است.

این ناوشکن ۲۱ نوامبر ۲۰۲۵، در قالب گروه رزمی ناو هواپیمابر «آبراهام لینکلن»، سن‌دیگو را ترک کرد. ماموریت آن ابتدا برای حدود هفت ماه برنامه‌ریزی شده بود، اما با آغاز جنگ علیه ایران تمدید شد و حتی پس از بازگشت ناو هواپیمابر آبراهام لینکلن، اسپروئنس در خاورمیانه باقی ماند.

به گفته نیروی دریایی آمریکا، این ناوشکن در طول ماموریت خود بیش از ۸۸ هزار مایل دریایی پیمود و در جریان جنگ با ایران، ده‌ها موشک تاماهاک به سوی اهداف نظامی شلیک کرد.

مقام‌های آمریکایی همچنین می‌گویند که اسپروئنس در جریان عملیات نظامی، ۱۲ پهپاد و چهار موشک کروز ضدکشتی را سرنگون کرده است.

ناوشکن اسپروئنس از جمله شناورهای آمریکایی بود که در نخستین روز جنگ، ۲۸ فوریه، در حملات موشکی به ایران مشارکت داشت.

در همان روز، مدرسه ابتدایی شجره طیبه در شهر میناب در استان هرمزگان هدف حمله قرار گرفت. به گفته مقام‌های ایرانی، بیش از ۱۷۵ نفر، از جمله شمار زیادی کودک، در این حمله کشته شدند.

خبرگزاری آسوشیتدپرس در ماه مارس گزارش داد که ناوشکن اسپروئنس در محدوده برد موشکی مدرسه میناب قرار داشت و فرماندهی مرکزی ارتش آمریکا، سنتکام، تصویری از شلیک موشک تاماهاک از این ناوشکن در روز ۲۸ فوریه منتشر کرده بود.

با این حال، هنوز مشخص نشده است که آیا موشک اصابت‌کرده به مدرسه میناب از همین ناوشکن شلیک شده بود یا نه.

بخش راستی‌آزمایی بی‌بی‌سی با بررسی تصاویر ویدئویی تایید کرد که یک موشک تاماهاک آمریکایی به مجموعه نظامی سپاه پاسداران در مجاورت مدرسه برخورد کرده است. بررسی‌های گروه تحقیقاتی بلینگکت نیز نشان داد که حملات به این مجموعه و مدرسه احتمالا در دست‌کم دو موج انجام شده بود.

رویترز پیش‌تر به نقل از مقام‌های آمریکایی گزارش داده بود که یافته‌های اولیه تحقیقات ارتش آمریکا از احتمال مسئولیت نیروهای این کشور در حمله به مدرسه حکایت دارد.

هیئت حقیقت‌یاب سازمان ملل متحد نیز در ماه سپتامبر اعلام کرد که دلایل معقولی برای انتساب حمله به مدرسه میناب به نیروهای آمریکایی وجود دارد و شواهد موجود می‌تواند نشان‌دهنده ارتکاب جنایت جنگی باشد.

مقام‌های آمریکایی یافته‌های این هیئت را رد کرده‌اند. گزارش نهایی تحقیقات وزارت دفاع آمریکا درباره حمله به مدرسه نیز به‌طور عمومی منتشر نشده است.

منبع تصویر، Corbis via Getty Images

ناوشکن اسپروئنس علاوه بر حملات موشکی به ایران، در عملیات دفاع در برابر پهپادها و موشک‌های ایرانی و همچنین محاصره دریایی بنادر ایران مشارکت داشت.

این ناوشکن در ماه آوریل یک کشتی باری ایرانی به نام «توسکا» را که به گفته سنتکام از دستور نیروهای آمریکایی برای توقف پیروی نکرده بود، هدف تیراندازی قرار داد.

ماموریت طولانی اسپروئنس در حالی پایان یافته است که ادامه استقرار ناوهای آمریکایی در خاورمیانه نگرانی‌هایی درباره فشار بر خدمه، فرسودگی تجهیزات و دشواری نگهداری از شناورهای جنگی ایجاد کرده است.

بازگشت این ناوشکن به سن‌دیگو، پایان یکی از طولانی‌ترین ماموریت‌های دریایی آمریکا در دهه‌های اخیر است؛ ماموریتی که بخش مهمی از آن با جنگ علیه ایران و عملیات نظامی در خاورمیانه همراه بود.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by ROBERTO SCHMIDT / AFP via Getty Images)

Marco Rubio reached back more than 2,000 years to a Roman general to warn the International Criminal Court (ICC) that its rulings carry no force over Americans.

The secretary of state delivered the message during a keynote to the Federalist Society’s National Lawyers Convention in Washington Friday, according to a State Department transcript.

The same answer the Roman commander Pompey once gave to those citing their city’s charters against his legions would greet any move to enforce the court’s decrees on U.S. citizens, Rubio stated. “Stop quoting laws to men with swords,” he said. The line drew laughter, and he joked that the words were not politically correct.

FULL REMARKS: Secretary of State Marco Rubio Delivers Keynote Address, Answers Questions at Federalist Society National Lawyers Convention https://t.co/I9Zbat5ZVY

Rubio accused the court and its global-bureaucracy allies of making themselves “judge and jury and executioner of the international order” while answering to no one, according to the transcript. The tribunal now claims the power to investigate, prosecute and jail Americans under rules the country never approved, he stated. (RELATED: Trump Admin Announces Sanctions Against International Criminal Court Chief)

The secretary cast international law itself as a weapon of a global elite, arguing that critics had wielded it against nearly every major foreign policy decision of the Trump administration, Agence France-Presse (AFP) reported. He pointed to the U.S. military’s strikes on cartel boats in the Caribbean and the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro as moves that drew such objections, and he turned the same scorn on the United Nations.

The address was Rubio’s first major speech at home since Republicans absorbed heavy losses in this month’s midterm elections, and the crowd met him with a standing ovation, AFP reported. His choice of a prominent legal audience fed new speculation about a 2028 presidential bid, according to the Hill.

The appearance followed the sweeping sanctions the administration placed on the court in October as part of a campaign it says will dismantle the tribunal, the Associated Press (AP) reported. Washington signed the treaty that created the ICC yet never ratified it, which leaves the United States outside the court alongside Israel, Russia and China, AFP reported.

Enforcement is where the court runs thin, since it fields no police force and leans on member nations to arrest anyone it indicts, AP reported. The United States is not one of them.

Rubio tied the fight to national identity in closing. “To submit to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats would be to betray who we are, to betray ourselves,” he stated in the remarks.

news.originalContent:
At least 11 employees at two of America’s most powerful intelligence and cyber warfare agencies have died by suicide over the past year, prompting scrutiny from Congress and the White House.

The deaths occurred among military personnel, civilian employees and contractors working for the National Security Agency (NSA) and U.S. Cyber Command, including five suicides within roughly one month that military officials classified as a suicide cluster, according to The Japan Times. The deaths have prompted congressional inquiries and new restrictions on working hours as the agencies grapple with mounting operational demands from overseas conflicts, although officials have not determined that workplace pressures caused the suicides.

The Pentagon referred the Daily Caller News Foundation to Cyber Command who did not respond for comment. The NSA also did not respond to the DCNF’s request for comment. (RELATED: ‘Leadership Doesn’t Know Anything Else’: Why Are Suicide Rates In US Military So High?)

“The pace of operations right now at both NSA and Cyber Command can be overwhelming,” said Harry Coker Jr., a former senior executive at the NSA and Central Intelligence Agency told The Japan Times. “There is a lot of stress that a lot of us overlook because we think cyber is away from the front, and physically that’s accurate but intellectually and emotionally it’s inaccurate.”

Stallings’ family remembered him as as a devoted and discreet officer. He loved riding his motorcycle, reading Green Lantern comics and his chihuahua, Scud. As a kid, he covered his bedroom with glow-in-the-dark stars and stayed up late, reading under the blankets by flashlight. https://t.co/41wtOy924W

From early June to early July, five employees at the NSA and Cyber Command took their lives. These were categorized as cluster suicides, a phenomenon defined as when “suicides or suicide attempts happen closer together in time, location, or both than expected,” per the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The most recent suicide was in September.

This timeline of this cluster coincides with America shifting from a fragile ceasefire agreement with Iran to renewed fighting, according to United States Central Command (CENTCOM).

Even as legislators and military officials made efforts towards addressing the unique mental health challenges faced by these personnel, the suicides continued. Of the ten suicides, nine took place in Fort Meade, Maryland and one in Georgia, according to The Japan Times.

Congressional committees overseeing the military and intelligence agencies requested briefings from both agencies regarding the suicides and workload stress. Tim Kosiba, the NSA’s deputy director, went to the White House to brief officials, per the outlet.

NSA and Cyber Command leaders said that each servicemember had distinctly different motives for ending their lives including personal and financial issues. Technical Sergeant Kevin Stallings referred to a “wall of debt,” his divorce, an earlier suicide in his military unit and the death of his dog, Scud, for his June 11 suicide. Stallings apologized to his military leaders in his suicide note, saying they could not have prevented it.

“This is something I would never reach out for,” he wrote in the note obtained by The Japan Times.

Gen. Joshua Rudd, the Cyber Command and NSA leader, requested $11 million in April to address personnel mental health, warning of possible “burnout and force degradation.”

Two lawmakers sent letters urging the approval of this request in October, following the string of suicides per The Japan Times.

“While we know a lot about warfare,” Democratic Maryland Rep. Sarah Elfreth said according to Bloomberg. “[W]e don’t know much about electronic warfare in terms of its impact on the psyche and people’s mental health.”

Shutterstock image via user Andrey Popov

Microsoft claimed early Saturday morning that the functionality of its Outlook email program has been restored for its 100 million users after a roughly 36-hour outage.

“We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the Microsoft 365 Status account announced on X at 1:09 a.m. EST. The outage occurred at approximately 11:17 a.m. EST Thursday, affecting 74 countries and territories within an hour, according to Downdetector. (RELATED: Microsoft Says Email Backlog ‘Approaching Normal’ After Outage Paralyzes Outlook)

“We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners,” a Microsoft spokesperson told the Daily Caller News Foundation. “We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.”

We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions. Further updates can be found at MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 products, according to Microsoft’s fiscal year 2025 third-quarter earnings call.

Along with affecting health services in the United Kingdom, law enforcement in Australia, and tax transactions in Singapore, the outage also appears to have affected legislative operations in Congress as it begins its lame-duck session, The New York Times reported Friday.

“We have seen improvements to Outlook’s functionality this morning, but will continue to monitor the situation until all issues are resolved and full functionality is restored to all Microsoft applications,” House Chief Administrative Officer spokeswoman Samantha Carter told the outlet.

“We all use Outlook, that’s our life, everything is there, our calendar is there, our boss’s calendar, so it has been a challenge … with no access to our Bible,” one House staffer reportedly told POLITICO. “There goes a day of legislative work.”

While Microsoft confirmed the outage was not caused by a cyberattack, the company has faced Microsoft 365 outages in January, July, and August of 2026.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters late Friday that Microsoft’s latest outage and the Federal Aviation Administration’s recent nationwide ground stop are “separate issues.”

Microsoft stated Friday it will release an incident report of the outage. It also stated the problem was introduced “during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change.”

Editor’s note: This breaking news report was updated with a statement from Microsoft.
news.content:
Shutterstock image via user Andrey Popov

Microsoft claimed early Saturday morning that the functionality of its Outlook email program has been restored for its 100 million users after a roughly 36-hour outage.

“We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions,” the Microsoft 365 Status account announced on X at 1:09 a.m. EST. The outage occurred at approximately 11:17 a.m. EST Thursday, affecting 74 countries and territories within an hour, according to Downdetector. (RELATED: Microsoft Says Email Backlog ‘Approaching Normal’ After Outage Paralyzes Outlook)

“We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners,” a Microsoft spokesperson told the Daily Caller News Foundation. “We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.”

We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions. Further updates can be found at MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

Over 430 million people use Microsoft 365 products, according to Microsoft’s fiscal year 2025 third-quarter earnings call.

Along with affecting health services in the United Kingdom, law enforcement in Australia, and tax transactions in Singapore, the outage also appears to have affected legislative operations in Congress as it begins its lame-duck session, The New York Times reported Friday.

“We have seen improvements to Outlook’s functionality this morning, but will continue to monitor the situation until all issues are resolved and full functionality is restored to all Microsoft applications,” House Chief Administrative Officer spokeswoman Samantha Carter told the outlet.

“We all use Outlook, that’s our life, everything is there, our calendar is there, our boss’s calendar, so it has been a challenge … with no access to our Bible,” one House staffer reportedly told POLITICO. “There goes a day of legislative work.”

While Microsoft confirmed the outage was not caused by a cyberattack, the company has faced Microsoft 365 outages in January, July, and August of 2026.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters late Friday that Microsoft’s latest outage and the Federal Aviation Administration’s recent nationwide ground stop are “separate issues.”

Microsoft stated Friday it will release an incident report of the outage. It also stated the problem was introduced “during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change.”

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Joel Angel Juarez/Getty Images)

Democrats’ major victories at the state level could lead to major changes on school choice, labor laws, abortion, healthcare and other key policy agendas.

Democrats flipped at least 549 state legislative seats, 12 state legislatures and broke Republican supermajorities in 13 chambers in the largest flip in state power since the Tea Party wave during the 2010 midterm elections, when former President Barack Obama held office. Democrats will use their new majorities to attempt making policy changes on data centers, Obamacare coverage and election integrity, among others.

Before the election, Republicans controlled the executive and the legislature trifecta in 21 states and Democrats held the same control in 14 states. After Election Day, Democrats are set to hold state trifectas in 20 states, while Republicans will hold the trifecta in 16 states. Nine states are divided, according to Ballotpedia.

“There’s probably going to be a major effort legislatively by the new progressive majorities to overturn some of the big conservative victories, whether it’s school choice or on labor issues or on taxes … In Georgia, where Democrats had a very good evening on the governor’s race and all the statewide races, there’s going to be a big debate around whether Georgia expands Obamacare and Medicaid,” Williams told the DCNF. “You’re going to have, I think, a real robust debate in that state being newly divided politically.”

Arizona, Michigan, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Nevada and Wisconsin have new Democratic trifectas, and they broke Republican trifectas in Georgia, New Hampshire, Iowa, Ohio and Texas, according to the National Conference of State Legislatures.

Medicaid and Affordable Care Act expansion was a central issue in the Georgia gubernatorial race, where Democratic Georgia Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms defeated former Republican Georgia gubernatorial nominee Rick Jackson. Democrats took control of the Georgia state House for the first time in over 20 years, holding 91 House seats. Republicans kept control of the state Senate. (RELATED: Democrat Scott Colom Wins Mississippi Senate Seat)

Georgia is roughly one of ten states that never fully adopted the Affordable Care Act’s Medicaid expansion and instead runs Georgia Pathways, which is set to expire in 2026. About 12% of the state’s population is uninsured, making Georgia one of the highest uninsured states in the country. Bottoms argued that full expansion would benefit rural hospitals and healthcare systems strained by uninsured patents relying on emergency rooms.

Bottoms and the Georgia state House could face hurdles with trying to pass the expansion in the state Senate, who will still hold a majority in January. The Georgia Republican Party’s post-election playbook states they will “negotiate any wider coverage on Georgia terms: work requirements and private plans.”

Some state Senate Republicans did not reject the idea of expanding coverage in interviews with The Georgia Recorder, a local outlet.

Democrats in the Texas state Legislature unveiled their plan to expand Medicaid under Obamacare in 2027. Their plan would direct the Texas Health and Human Services Commission to submit a federal plan to expand Medicaid. Texas is the most populous state to not allow Medicaid expansion.

Democrats acknowledged this would face pushback in the Texas state Senate, where Republicans will keep control.

Democrats took control of the Texas state House for the first time since 2003. Democratic Texas Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa defeated Republican Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, making her the first Democrat to win a Texas gubernatorial race since former President George W. Bush became governor in 1994.

Democratic Texas state Rep. Donna Howard filed an omnibus bill Monday to repeal the state’s abortion ban and other related statues, according to KRGV 5 News, a local ABC News affiliate. Abortion is banned at all stages of pregnancy under state law with exception to save the mother’s life.

Abortion laws are likely to change in Iowa and North Carolina, where abortion is restricted at six and 12 weeks.

Hinojosa campaigned on establishing an immediate moratorium on new data centers and tied Abbott to the tech industry throughout her campaign. Abbott pledged to make Texas the “epicenter” of artificial intelligence development, but ordered state agencies to halt permits for new construction, which Hinojosa alleged was a political move.

Abbott raked in $26 million in a 30-day reporting period that ended Oct. 24, with at least $6 million coming from Space X and Tesla CEO Elon Musk and other donors associated with tech and data centers, according to Politico.

Democrats and Republicans in the Texas state Legislature filed a handful of bills to repeal the sales and use tax exemption for data centers, according to KRGV 5. Many state legislators expressed support for a handful of restrictions on data centers, which Hinojosa is likely to sign into law if they reached her desk.

Newly elected Pennsylvania Democrats campaigned on their opposition to data centers. In the next legislative session, Democrats said they want to address electric grid costs, codify data center regulations and study environmental impacts. Many bills that did not pass in the current Legislature could be reintroduced, including one that would propose a three-year statewide moratorium.

Democratic Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro signed an executive order on Aug. 18 to establish stricter guardrails on data centers.

Progressive Democrats in Arizona, Iowa, Nevada and Wisconsin aggressively pushed back against data centers.

New progressive majorities in the state governments will likely try to tackle policies considered major conservative victories, such as school choice and right to work laws, Williams said.

Hinojosa expressed opposition to the Texas Education Freedom Accounts program, the state’s $1 billion private school voucher system, and has promised to redirect state education dollars back into public schools. She announced plans to fire Texas Education Agency (TEA) Commissioner Mike Morath on her first day in office and replace him with an educator to pivot state policy toward public schools.

The Republican-held state Senate in Texas is unlikely to support these efforts.

Democratic Iowa Gov.-elect Rob Sand expressed similar concerns on private school choice programs, expressing concerns about the policies disproportionately benefitting the wealthy. Iowa’s state Legislature will still be held by a Republican majority.

Williams said Democratic trifectas will likely attempt to reverse or weaken right-to-work laws and expand union organizing rights. He pointed to Democratic Wisconsin Gov.-elect David Crowley, who pledged to repeal Wisconsin’s right-to-work laws and overturn Act 10, a 2011 law that restricted collective bargaining for most public employees.

Democrats may work to redraw the lines in states where they took control of the trifectas, including Wisconsin, where Crowley said he would sign a bill redrawing the map if it reached his desk. He argued that will not become a central issue in a state like Arizona, which has a nonpartisan commission to draw its maps.

Arizona Democrats would like to repeal Republican-led voter access laws. Many would like to restore the state’s Permanent Early Voting List, which automatically sent a mail-in ballot to voters who opted in, according to the Arizona Mirror, a local outlet. Former Republican Arizona Gov. Doug Ducey signed a law in 2021 requiring voters to be removed from the list if they did not cast a mail-in ballot for two consecutive cycles.

Texas Democrats could take up bills to allow online voter registration, mail-in voting and to require polling places on college campuses.

Despite the major gains for Democrats, many voters enshrined policies that took the states in a conservative direction even after voting for Democrats, Williams told the DCNF. Voters sided with conservatives in many ballot referendums, including a California initiative that would have instituted a 5% tax on the wealth of billionaires to raise tens of billions in revenue to address education services, health, nutrition and other services.

DDHQ Race Update (est. 47% in): California Proposition 40 - One-Time Wealth Tax for State-Funded Healthcare, Education, and Food Assistance Programs No (N): 2,934,565 (56.8%) Yes (N): 2,228,236 (43.2%) Follow more results here: https://t.co/dtMno7w7P0 https://t.co/aCdTthiVKx

Voters passed a constitutional amendment to increase the homestead tax exemption for non-school taxes to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. It would give new Florida residents a smaller initial exemption until they have lived in the state for five years and restrict counties and municipalities to spending property tax revenue on public safety, education, natural resource projects and infrastructure.

Idaho voters rejected a measure that would have legalized abortion up to fetal viability. They approved an initiative to constitutionally designate English as the state’s official language.

“I predict in many of these new majority states for the Democrats, they’ll move very quickly in order to pursue their agenda, and you’re going to see some major battles emerge in the opening days of 2027 in many of these state capitals,” Williams continued.

Voters soured on Republicans at the national and state level over their handling of the affordability crisis, prompting major victories in state trifectas. Williams was skeptical that new Democratic-led legislatures will address affordability, which he said could have negative implications for them in 2028.

“I think voters are in for a real unfortunate set of circumstances here as affordability won’t be tackled,” Williams told the DCNF. “You look at Virginia under Abigail Spanberger, who ran on the exact same affordability platform a year ago against Winsome Sears, and one of the things that Governor Spanberger now has pursued in their first session were tax increases, the regional greenhouse gas initiative to make electricity more expensive and to basically take our electricity standards and tie them to California standards. And so, if the playbook is California and the playbook is the affordability campaign from a year ago in Virginia, I’m not very optimistic that affordability is going to be tackled by these new progressive majorities.”

news.originalContent: The IDF addressed the strikes carried out overnight in southern Lebanon, including in the village of Kfar Reman, saying on Monday afternoon that they began after Hezbollah terrorists launched two explosive drones at Israeli forces on the Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon. No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility.   No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility. A vehicle in which two people were killed. The Associated Press reported that the vehicle belonged to the Lebanese Scout and Rescue Association, Al-Risala, and that one of those killed was a paramedic with the organization. Two other people were wounded. At the same time, Lebanese reports said a building in Kfar Reman where a large number of people were staying was also struck, killing nine people, including women and children, and wounding 11 others.   Prior to the strikes, steps were taken to mitigate harm to uninvolved individuals, including the use of precise munitions and aerial surveillance," the IDF said in response. "The claim that several uninvolved individuals were harmed as a result of the strikes is being reviewed.” The IDF said that, in addition, following the launch of the explosive drones Sunday, “the IDF struck in the Nabatieh area and eliminated several Hezbollah terrorists. "The IDF will not allow the Hezbollah terrorist organization to harm Israeli civilians or IDF soldiers and will continue to operate to remove threats while remaining committed to the ceasefire agreement." “We lived under constant intimidation because of the bombardments on the outskirts of the village,” Fouad Chakroun, a resident of Kfar Reman told AP as he stood in front of the destroyed building. “Now they have struck the heart of the village.” Another resident, Saleh Madlij, said families and children had been staying in the building. “Are there missiles here?” he said sarcastically. “I will not leave this place.” The BBC reported that, according to Lebanese media, seven additional people were killed in strikes Sunday, while Lebanese President Joseph Aoun warned that the attacks represented a “dangerous escalation” that threatened the ceasefire.

news.originalContent: Senior government officials admit that Israel's public opinion in the international community "has never been worse." According to them, the situation only worsens, and the support the world has shown Israel following Hamas’s attack on October 7 has already been forgotten.  Follow Ynetnews on Facebook | Twitter | Instagram | TikTok >> More stories: IDF releases name of fallen soldier in West Bank terror attack UN chief in Rafah crossing says world 'seen enough' of Gaza war Two Air Force pilots reminisce about their murdered brothers: 'There's no room for pain in the air' The officials added that the intensity of accusations made against Israel only increases, and attempts to equate Hamas's actions in Israel are being made, with allegations accusing IDF soldiers of sexually harassing Palestinian prisoners. Ministers in the government blame Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the complete neglect of Israel’s public relations: "There’s no leader present it’s been abandoned. A pandemic of sanctions against Israel may break out, and if we don't wake up, it will be too late. Something big needed to be done in terms of public relations, we need to rally the Jewish people and launch an international campaign. There’s no leader to head this. We’re losing. Our friends tell us: we support you, but you’re losing in the court of public opinion." A senior figure in Israel's advocacy efforts added, "They neutralized the Foreign Ministry and took away all its budget. The Foreign Ministry has no funding. To this day, no money was delivered. We’re working with a budget of 2 million shekels allocated for the war since the beginning of the year.  “Each U.S. consulate receives $5,000 a year for public relations efforts, including Independence Day events. For example, the consulate in Boston, which is also responsible for MIT, has to struggle to have such an amount. It’s ridiculous. When you already have a talented spokesman like Eylon Levy, they unjustly suspend him. He was one of the few people who did his mission in the most talented, beautiful, and correct way, and they sent him home,” the source said.   Internal reports from Israeli missions in the United States describe a very harsh picture of Israeli coverage in the American media. One report described, "The media awaited a sign from the government for a policy change, and when it arrived - it unleashed a rampage and published constant harsh criticism against Israel that had always existed. The harsh reports from Gaza, alongside internal tensions in the U.S., threaten to push moderate writers from the mainstream to adopt critical positions toward Israel and demand an immediate and permanent cease-fire.” 'the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy' “Pressure on the Biden administration to harden its stance toward Israel and condition military aid for an Israeli policy change constitutes a warning sign for the future,” the report added. “In terms of 'color,' we’re currently in a 'dark orange.' “There’s a change in stances even among staunch supporters of Israel – and while the conservative media fully supported Israel's actions in the past, this time voices questioning the proportionality of Israeli action have also been heard. However, no demand for a cease-fire is expected to appear in those media outlets. Without a fundamental change in the humanitarian issue in Gaza and/or signs on the diplomatic solution on the horizon, criticism of Israel in the media is expected to intensify,” the report read. It was added, "In the last month, the U.S. media’s spotlight turned to the worsening humanitarian crisis in Gaza, with special emphasis given to the suffering of Rafah residents against the backdrop of the possibility of the IDF expanding the ground operation there as well. Leading media outlets flooded screens and front pages with images of starving children, trauma victims, and the destruction of homes and hospitals. Reports and personal stories from Rafah led to empathy toward the Palestinians’ suffering and anger toward Israel's military actions. "Although most media outlets refrained from blaming Israel for creating the crisis intentionally or denying its right to self-defense, opinion pieces sparked fierce debate regarding the proportionality and morality of the ongoing military operation in its current form. Critical voices that were once silenced now have a wider platform.    “Reports focused on the immense humanitarian damages and the harm to innocent civilians, which many analysts argue is unjustified and goes against the values of the IDF’s operation. Even publicists who supported Israel in the past admitted that the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy,” the report read. “Against this backdrop, a narrative is emerging among liberal authors, which sees the Biden administration and its policy of providing weapons and diplomatic support to Israel as responsible for the situation, or at least as someone who can bring it to an end." Furthermore, dozens of recent opinion pieces represent a wide range of positions regarding the IDF’s legitimacy, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, the question of a cease-fire, and the future of U.S.-Israel relations: Conservative media outlets like The Wall Street Journal and The New York Post fully support Israel, advocate for continued military action against Hamas, and refrain from calling for an immediate and prolonged stop to the war.  In contrast, newspapers identified with the center and liberal left, including The New York Times and The Washington Post, criticize the war’s escalation, citing the destructive consequences of the confrontation on Palestinian civilians, and therefore calling for an immediate humanitarian cease-fire, the reports explained.   The reports also expose an erosion of Israel's standing in Washington against the backdrop of the escalation in the Gaza war. This was clearly reflected in U.S. President Joe Biden's statement regarding a "red line" on military operations in Rafah, and Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech.  Most analysts don’t foresee an immediate shift in relations between the countries, but caution against potential political damage to both sides. Furthermore, calls are increasing to use American military aid to Israel as leverage to force policy change in Jerusalem. However, warnings have been raised that the fact of having this discussion could bolster Hamas's position and undermine the chances of a cease-fire.  While conservative media outlets present Israel's policy as legitimate self-defense, liberal media outlets provide a platform for writers who echo the Palestinian narrative, sometimes using rhetoric accusing Israel of "apartheid" and even "genocide." Calls for the U.S. government to distance itself from supporting Israel and reconsider its military aid plan are becoming more common, even in moderate media outlets. The report mentions articles in The Washington Post and The Daily Beast highlighting the effectiveness of pro-Palestinian activists in influencing public opinion in the U.S., especially among progressive Democratic voters. The articles point to growing discontent with the Biden administration's support for Israel, reflected in "Uncommitted" votes in the Democratic primaries and disruptions at party events. Tactics such as demanding a cease-fire and using the term "genocide" have succeeded in keeping the war at the forefront of the national political agenda and increasing pressure on Washington to minimize its support of Israel.  The increasing willingness of Democratic politicians to criticize Israel suggests a shift in the party's traditional stance and leads to speech free of restraint in media outlets as well. This trend reached its zenith with Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech, in which he labeled Netanyahu an "obstacle to peace" and accused him of damaging Israel's international standing, calling for early Israeli elections.

news.title: 'We are in Shock': British Jews react to fatal terror attack - and fume at the 'lax response' of the UK
news.originalSummary: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities. news.originalContent: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities.   Follow Ynetnews on Facebook and Twitter >> Related stories: Israel names two sisters killed in West Bank terror attack At least one dead and six injured in a terror attack in Tel Aviv Family loses two daughters to deadly terror attack Members of the Jewish London community, including friends of the family, who heard of the devastating news after the Shabbat ended, were confronted only then, with the horrific reports of Maia and Rina's death. The funerals for the Dee sisters will be held today at the Kfar Etzion Cemetery.   Rabbi Leo Dee served as the Assistant Rabbi at the Hendon United Synagogue in North London from 2008-2011, and as the Senior Rabbi at Radlett United Synagogue from 2011-2014, after which the family made aliyah. They were a much beloved and respected family in the UK Jewish community. “People feel shock and disappointment. The family were communal people and served their communities well and were well-liked.” said a former member of the congregation at Hendon United Synagogue who did not wish to be named.  “I feel sick seeing this… good people who would never hurt anyone, murdered. I can't imagine his anguish, and pray Lucy survives,” said Joseph, another former congregant.   Chief UK Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis laments the death of the British-Israeli girls murdered in Friday's terror strike on the West Bank.  In a statement, the rabbi said: "No words can describe the depth of our shock and sadness at the heartbreaking news of the murder by terrorists in Israel of Maya & Rina Dee, daughters of Rebbetzen Lucy, who is in a critical condition & Rabbi Leo Dee, my dear colleagues. He continued, “They were much loved in the Hendon and Radlett communities in the UK, as well as in Israel and well beyond.” UK statement not mentioning terrorism The British Board of Deputies also issued a statement expressing shock over the tragic attack: “We are deeply shocked and saddened at the murder by Palestinian terrorists of Maia and Rina Dee, the daughters of Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee formerly of Radlett United Synagogue. We wish Lucy Refuah Shlemah and long life to the family as they cope with this devastating news.” Palestinian terrorist shot and killed 2 British-Israeli nationals, also critically injuring their mother in the West Bank. The victims were identified Saturday as 15-year-old Rina Dee and 20-year-old Maia Dee, the daughters of British-born Rabbi Leo Dee.  While their mother, Lucy (Lea), remains in critical condition fighting for her life, the Jewish community in the UK has expressed shock and sorrow at the brutal act of terrorism against former members of their community.    While many Jewish community leaders spoke out about the attack, the UK government has received criticism from some members of the community for its weakly-worded response to the killing of two of its own citizens.  One member of the Jewish community told Ynet that it was shocking that the UK statement didn’t even mention terrorism. “The response would be different if this happened elsewhere in the world. There is a double standard for British people killed in Israel,” he said.  The UK’s official statement read: “We are saddened to hear about the deaths of two British-Israeli citizens and the serious injuries sustained by a third individual. The UK calls for all parties across the region to de-escalate tensions.” "Tragedy for global Jewish community" Avi Abelow, family friend, said Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee are beloved and active members of their community in Efrat. "Two of the sweetest people with the sweetest children", he added. "Rabbi Leo continues to teach Torah classes in his Efrat synagogue today. All the youth of Efrat, as their families, are mourning the loss of either their personal friend or the sibling of their personal friend."  He mentioned that "Just last night the whole community got together, including many youth, for a special communal prayer gathering to pray for Lucy's recovery. The brutal Arab Muslim terrorist attack that murdered these two young, innocent Jewish women, and seriously injured their mother fighting for her life, is not just a tragedy for their family, but for the whole Efrat community and the global Jewish community.  "At the same time that another terrorist committed a terror attack in Tel Aviv, which killed an Italian tourist, and terrorist organizations are shooting rockets at Israel from Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, we are once again reminded that the Jewish people have enemies trying to kill us everywhere in our country for just being Jews living in our ancestral homeland.  "If only the UK government and other global bodies would recognize this truth, and truly give support to Israel to stop this ongoing terror war against Israel, which causes loss of life for everyone. In the meantime, as a personal friend and neighbor of the Dee family, my family, neighbors, and community will continue to assist and comfort the Dee family, as we assisted and comforted the family of our other friend and neighbor, Ari Fuld, murdered by terrorists back in 2018."

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Apparently, 60 minutes of football wasn’t enough for Louisville and North Carolina on Saturday night.

The two ACC rivals decided to throw in a little extracurricular activity after the final whistle, turning an already heated contest into a full-blown postgame brawl.

Louisville escaped with a 16-14 victory over Bill Belichick’s Tar Heels, but the final score quickly became an afterthought when both sidelines emptied onto the field in a chaotic scene that looked more like a handful of heavyweight boxing matches than the conclusion of a college football game.

We got a brawl at the end of the Louisville vs UNC game pic.twitter.com/nIeyCwJuOc

The trouble began after North Carolina quarterback Travis Burgess threw a costly interception with just over a minute remaining, effectively ending the Tar Heels’ hopes of stealing a victory.

Louisville needed only to kneel down and run out the clock. Instead, the Cardinals’ final kneel-down became the opening bell for an all-out fight between the two teams.

Players began exchanging words before tempers boiled over, sending teammates pouring off both sidelines as pushing and shoving escalated into a sprawling melee.

Officials desperately blew their whistles and tossed penalty flags, although expecting a few yellow pieces of laundry to stop dozens of furious football players seemed about as effective as bringing a squirt gun to a burning building.

news.originalContent:
Substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto’s late goal helps Japan avenge their defeat by Brazil in the World Cup round of 32.

Brazil forward Raphinha and manager Carlo Ancelotti were shown red cards for protesting against a referee’s decision in the South American giant’s shock defeat to Japan in a thrilling friendly match in Singapore.

Substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto netted his first international goal with a late winner on Saturday as Japan edged Brazil 3-2 at the National Stadium.

A brilliant brace by Vinicius Jr had erased a two-goal deficit after strikes by Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura put the Samurai Blue 2-0 up in the opening 19 minutes.

But Sakamoto was in the right place to fire home after latching on to Kodai Sano’s deflected effort in stoppage time to give the Asian side a dramatic victory in front of 38,688 people.

Brazil appealed for a foul in the build-up to the goal, but VAR upheld the goal, and Raphinha and manager Ancelotti were shown red cards for their protests.

Ancelotti seemed surprised at the decision while Raphinha was led away by midfielder Marlon Gomes and team officials as he tried to approach referee Jansen Foo, who was instead confronted by Vinicius and Bruno Guimaraes.

“The referee gave me a red card because he said I wasn’t able to control the bench and that all the players were on the field,” Ancelotti said at a news conference.

“It’s a shame about the result because we don’t like to lose the game, but we have to look at what we did well. There are many positives. Some players who played for the first time showed good quality. For 70 minutes, the team played well.

“The result, obviously, was influenced by the referee’s performance, … but it’s not his fault. It was a high-level match, and I don’t think he had the experience to handle this kind of game.”

Raphinha was still fuming over the “unacceptable” red card as he critiqued the referee’s decisions while speaking to reporters after the match.

“First of all, I’d like to take this opportunity to apologise for my behaviour and for being sent off,” Raphinha said.

“Sometimes it’s hard to keep calm, especially after what I felt were so many refereeing errors during the match. I tried to speak to him several times, and not once did I feel he was open to discussion. I believe that he made many errors throughout the game, and that is unacceptable,” the Brazil captain said.

“In my view, their first goal involved a foul when the opponent took the ball off me with his hand. I think it’s a foul, but I can understand why it wasn’t given based on the current law. Then there was the penalty in the first half. In my opinion, it was a penalty, but he said no.

“Then, for their third goal, there was a clear foul on Joao Gomes. With the help of VAR, he eventually allowed the goal. It’s very difficult not to talk about the refereeing.”

The victory carried added significance for Japan, who suffered a heartbreaking exit to Brazil in the World Cup last 32 in June. On that occasion, Gabriel Martinelli struck in stoppage time to complete a 2-1 comeback win for the South Americans.

“I’m happy that I can say that today’s match was the best match in my eight-year tenure,” Japan head coach Hajime Moriyasu said after the game.

“Brazil’s intensity went up once we took the lead, and it was all about what we could do then.

“Our players performed at the world’s top standard. These wins lead to victories at the World Cup, and I hope they continue to do the same,” Moriyasu added.

The 58-year-old is expected to step down after a friendly against Paraguay on Tuesday and said he is looking forward to handing over to successor Go Oiwa.

“Now I need to pass the baton to the next coach, and that’s all I am focusing on.”

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Phil Collins gave a tearful acceptance speech and got an electrifying tribute from Cynthia Erivo, Oprah Winfrey inducted the late Luther Vandross, and Wu-Tang Clan made the Peacock Theater a rowdy celebration at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony on Saturday night.

Queen Latifah, Oasis, MC Lyte and Sade were also inducted, and Billy Idol, New Order and Iron Maiden were set to enter the hall later in the evening.

Collins, whose mobility issues and other health problems kept him from performing, took the stage slowly using a pair of canes and cried at a huge ovation from a crowd that included his daughter, actor Lily Collins.

Blink-182 drummer Travis Barker inducted Collins and praised him for his unprecedented dual stardom as a drummer and a hit-making pop singer in the 1980s.

“I grew up just wanting to play the drums,” Collins said. “Everything else has been a really happy accident. I can’t believe, when I look back, how life has gone.”

Barker said Collins’ song “In the Air Tonight” gave the world “arguably the most badass drum fill of all time.”

Minutes later, Barker played that fill himself as Erivo gave a slowed-down, epic rendition of the song that brought the crowd to its feet.

Collins was already in the hall as a member of Genesis, but now gets the solo honor.

He hasn’t been able to take the stage since 2022, but assured the crowd that “you haven’t heard the last of me.”

Winfrey, whose presence was unannounced, said with relish that Vandross was “the maestro of the love song” and said he was once correctly named “the top artist that people make looove to.”

Vandross, an R&B singer with a velvet voice, was one of the definitive singers of the 1980s and ’90s. He died in 2005.

“Luther Vandross sang with such passion and soul it could reach something deep inside that you didn’t even know needed to be reached,” Winfrey said.

Usher then took the stage and sang a sultry medley of Vandross hits, including “Here and Now” and “So Amazing.”

Wu-Tang Clan, the epic hip-hop collective from New York’s Staten Island, filled the stage with its 10 current members, giving a memorable acceptance speech and a performance that had the crowd on its feet and dancing.

Backed by a big jazz band, the musical medley included “C.R.E.A.M.,” “Method Man” and late member Ol’ Dirty Bastard’s “Shimmy Shimmy Ya.”

“Wu-Tang rewrote the rules of hip-hop and did it without a big machine behind them,” said comedian Chris Rock, who inducted them.

“We took Staten Island to the world,” the group’s leader RZA said. “We had a desire to conquer.”

He added, “We wanted to make a mark. We made our mark.”

MC Lyte, a trailblazing female rapper starting in the late 1980s, was the first artist inducted, with hip-hop star Remy Ma doing the honors and calling her “one of the first women in hip-hop to make sure there was room for the rest of us.”

MC Lyte said she was a “B-girl from Brooklyn just looking for my chance to inspire and motivate.” She did not perform at the moment of her induction but may be part of an ensemble later in the evening.

Her contemporary and fellow groundbreaker Latifah was inducted later in the evening by Megan Thee Stallion, who said Latifah “taught us to recognize royalty within ourselves.”

Latifah wore a leather crown that matched her leather trenchcoat and tie. She said, for a long time, she would not have believed this night was possible.

“It’s difficult enough being a woman in hip-hop, let alone being a hip-hopper in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame,” she said.

Latifah and MC Lyte then took the stage together to perform a medley of their hits, including Latifah’s “U.N.I.T.Y.” and Lyte’s “Ruffneck,” as members of Wu-Tang and Chuck D of Public Enemy danced and rapped along in the audience.

Latifah and Lyte entered the hall as recipients of the Early Influence Award along with posthumous nominees Gram Parsons, Fela Kuti and Celia Cruz.

U2 was the night’s surprise opener, playing their new single “Silencio” while surrounded by dancers in riot squad gear with helmets and shields. They then launched into their 1984 classic “Pride (In the Name of Love).”

Singer Bono alternately raised a peace sign and fist as guitarist the Edge and the rest of the band played the song about Martin Luther King, Jr. on the stage at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. U2 was inducted into the hall in 2005.

Oasis, the youngest of the inductees, didn’t show up. Guitarist Noel Gallagher is playing a gig back home in Britain, and his little brother, Liam Gallagher, just didn’t want to come.

“Anybody surprised they didn’t show up?” asked actor and Oasis superfan Bob Odenkirk, who inducted them. ”It would’ve been out of character if they had. I would’ve been worried about them.”

He praised their “bangers that make you sing along even before you finish hearing them for the first time,” before singer-songwriter Stephen Wilson Jr. gave an acoustic rendition of “Wonderwall.”

Sade also decided to skip the induction. The singer and her band that’s named after her were inducted by singer Andra Day and celebrated by singer Sienna Spiro, who sang the group’s beloved hit “Smooth Operator.”

Iron Maiden, to be inducted later Saturday night, was on tour in Australia. Key members of New Order, getting a joint induction with their previous incarnation Joy Division, will also be out for health reasons.

The show is in Los Angeles for the second straight year, and organizers have said it will be here more often while still rotating to New York and Cleveland, where the actual hall resides.

After streaming the ceremony live the past few years, the Rock Hall returned to its previous model, where the public won’t see it until an edited version airs on ABC and Disney+ on Dec. 9.

MEMPHIS, Tenn. — The Nets had to play without their leading scorer Saturday, as Michael Porter Jr. sat on the bench in street clothes.

He watched his team take a 129-110 beating in Memphis at FedExForum.

Porter wasn’t injured but was a healthy scratch for personal reasons.

Two sources — one a team source and another close to the player — said the issue was believed to be resolved and Porter shouldn’t miss extended time.

When asked if he had a timeline for Porter’s return, Nets coach Jordi Fernández said, “No. We want to give him his privacy. Everything is fine, so we’re happy that he was here.”

Initially listed as questionable, Porter was ruled out an hour before tipoff.

“A personal situation came up as we were coming to the arena. So that’s why it was announced late,” Fernández said.

Porter is averaging a team-high 21.5 points on 45.6 percent shooting and 37.5 percent from deep. An Eastern Conference scout who spoke with The Post pointed out how easy the Nets are to defend without his unblockable shot. Julius Randle — Brooklyn’s other proven veteran scorer — said others simply have to pick up the slack.

“Everybody has to step in and chip in. It’s not just one person,” Randle said. “So we’ve all got to step up and chip in and do it collectively as a unit.”

Day’Ron Sharpe (16 points, 11 rebounds, five assists) had his third double-double of the season already. His career high is six in 2023-24.

Fernández handed Noah Clowney the start at small forward for Porter. With Randle, Sharpe, Egor Dëmin and Danny Wolf, every Nets starter was at least 6-foot-9 or taller, just as they had been in the blowout win in New Orleans three nights earlier.

This was the first time any NBA team had started a lineup of players all 6-foot-9 or taller since the Los Angeles Lakers had done so April 21, 1990.

Mikel Brown Jr. and Nolan Traore both returned after having missed the blowout win in New Orleans three nights earlier. It marked just the third game that the Nets have had Dëmin, Brown and Traore together.

Fernández said Brown is still on his minutes limit. With Wolf still starting at two-guard, Brown and Traore logged just 19 minutes each.

The Nets got thrown into travel chaos Friday by the Federal Aviation Administration’s decision to ground every flight nationwide for four hours. They were already set to board their flight but had to stay overnight in New Orleans and fly to Memphis at 9 a.m.

“Yeah, obviously it was something that we couldn’t control,” Fernández said. “And to be honest with you, it was not that bad. We had good rest and got here [Saturday] morning and did our walk-through, and probably [would have] gone to the gym, but we were not able to. And I think we feel good and ready to go.”

news.originalContent:

ANAHEIM, Calif. — The Islanders had Mathew Barzal back for Saturday’s match against the Ducks but operated with caution regarding immediate expectations for him.

“Obviously he’s gotta transition back into full speed,” coach Pete DeBoer said before the 6-2 win. “We’re gonna work him into that, but it’s great that he’s available to play.”

What that means on a practical level is the Islanders will manage Barzal’s ice time closely — including 16:21 on Saturday. He’ll also start on the second power-play unit as opposed to the top group.

Jean-Gabriel Pageau missed a second straight game with a lower-body injury, and Calum Ritchie remains out with a lower-body injury, so there’s still some suspense over what the lineup will look like when fully healthy. Saturday, though, Barzal skated in Pageau’s usual spot on the third line between Ondrej Palat and Anthony Duclair, with no changes to the Islanders top six.

Matthew Kessel, who played as the seventh defenseman against the Kings two nights prior, was the healthy scratch, with the Islanders going back to a 12-forward, six-defenseman configuration.

“I’m not sure [what to expect], honestly, it’s been a while,” Barzal said. “So obviously I’m just excited. I know how I am. I know that when I get out there, I’m gonna want to play. I’m gonna want to be going over the boards a ton. We gotta be controlled, and the team’s been playing well. Just trying to hop in, bring what I bring. I know as soon as I hit that ice, I’m gonna want to go.”

DeBoer declined to commit to a number for Barzal’s minutes when asked, but it did seem clear that the 20:39 he averaged a year ago wasn’t going to be in the cards right away.

“He’s getting back in, he’s playing his first game in six or seven months,” DeBoer said. “We’re gonna manage his ice time, and we know there’s gonna be some runway here where he’s gotta work himself back into game shape and game timing. But it’s gonna be a great first step.”

Kyle MacLean was put on non-roster waivers to make room for Barzal. If he clears, he’ll likely be sent down to AHL Hamilton.

“That’s a tough conversation. Great pro, great kid, great man,” DeBoer said. “… He’s been a great, great Islander here. Been a lot of heavy lifting and work for a long time, so those are always tough.”

Ritchie (lower body) has started to skate on his own back in New York.

Logan Stanley left the game with a lower-body injury early in the second period and did not return. DeBoer said he would be evaluated Sunday upon the team’s return to New York.

news.originalContent:
Energy disruptions as a result of the US-Israel war on Iran is a key issue for the import-dependent bloc.

Southeast Asian countries that comprise the ASEAN economic bloc will meet in the Philippines this week as the region continues to bear the brunt of oil shortages caused by the US-Israel war on Iran, as well as by US-China rivalry, which has hit economies hard.

The Manila summit will be held from November 15 to 17 and will include US President Donald Trump and several other world leaders.

The 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) aims to establish a single market, although it cannot impose decisions on members. It comprises Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, Cambodia and East Timor, with a combined population of nearly 694 million, or 8.4 percent of the world’s population.

Several ASEAN meetings are held annually. This week’s summit is expected to be the final one for this year.

Beyond the energy crisis, other pressing issues include disputes over the South China Sea and trade.

In addition to leaders and representatives from the 11 member countries, other guests include:

The summit is being held at a time when Southeast Asian countries have been hit hard by shortages in oil and gas supplies from Middle Eastern suppliers amid the US-Israel war on Iran.

The Philippines, Vietnam and Malaysia are among the most vulnerable to the energy disruptions in the Gulf, with Manila declaring a state of national energy emergency in March.

Millions of ASEAN citizens also live and work in the Middle East, where the war threatens their safety and earnings.

Meanwhile, Asian countries are worried the conflict could spill into the Strait of Malacca, a narrow waterway between Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore.

The US’s tariff war has seen ASEAN countries slapped with 10-12.5 percent tariff hikes since the beginning of US President Donald Trump’s second term in the White House, prompting the bloc to strengthen trade relationships elsewhere.

China and four ASEAN members – Brunei, Malaysia, the Philippines and Vietnam – as well as Taiwan, have been locked in decades of territorial standoffs in the busy waterway.

The area is important as it is believed to host undersea deposits of oil and gas.

In 2005, the bloc began negotiating a “code of conduct” with China to discourage aggression and prevent major clashes. The negotiations have often stalled, however, partly due to flared tensions, especially between Manila and Beijing in recent years.

In 2023, the two sides agreed to speed things up and release a finished draft this year. At least 10 rounds of talks have been held this year, led by Malaysia, with a final round taking place in October.

However, analysts doubt a definite conclusion will be reached at the summit this week, meaning talks could continue into next year.

Armed clashes broke out between the two ASEAN member states late last year along an 800km (500-mile) contested border area, as well as over competing claims to sacred religious sites, such as the Preah Vihear Shiva temple.

At least 150 people were reported to have been killed, and nearly one million displaced.

ASEAN members, as well as China and the US, intervened, leading to talks. Although a ceasefire has been in place since December, the wider border dispute remains unresolved, and the bloc is calling for more dialogue and the participation of third-party observers.

The ongoing civil war in Myanmar, which has compounded the Rohingya refugee crisis, has been at the top of the agenda as the bloc pushes for the restoration of democracy in the country.

Multiple rebel forces, some of them ethnic-based armed groups, have been fighting the military government since the country’s February 2021 coup.

ASEAN has already restricted Myanmar’s participation at important summits to non-political representatives as concerns about violence and a humanitarian crisis grow.

The bloc’s five-point Myanmar peace plan, launched in April 2021 and calling for dialogue and improved humanitarian aid access, has meanwhile failed to alleviate the situation.

Months of widespread wildfires in drought-hit Indonesia have scorched an estimated 2.88 million hectares (7.12 million acres) and resulted in at least 3,500 deaths.

The resulting haze has severely impacted not just the country’s residents, but also those in neighbouring Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and East Timor.

Jakarta has faced criticism for failing to effectively respond to the fires, but the government has defended its approach, saying thousands of responders have been deployed.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

There was no joy at Madison Square Garden by the end of the night, only vocal displeasure with who was deemed the winner of the UFC 334 heavyweight title fight.

The fans wanted Josh Hokit to take the belt off Ciryl Gane on Saturday night (which bled into Sunday). The three judges had other ideas, awarding unanimous 48-47 scorecards.

“I will rejoice in my suffering. Suffering builds endurance. And endurance builds hope,” said Hokit afterward in the Octagon, absent his typical ugly brashness on the mic in the wake of his first career loss.

Hokit, an overwhelming darling of the Garden crowd, immediately shot for and secured a single-leg takedown, but Gane managed to get back to striking distance. Hokit’s frantic pressure made the Muay Thai striker from France less comfortable than normal but still more successful in landing punches against the brawling American, though Hokit in turn found his successes.

Gane again got snatched up for a more thunderous takedown late in the first frame, this time atop the center logo, and Hokit added some strikes for good measure to end a competitive opening round.

Hokit shot again to start the second, but Gane was finally ready for it and deftly defended. The uppercut, a solid weapon in the first, was again landing for Gane, and followed up in combination as Hokit’s frenetic energy settled.

But Gane noticeably had slowed by the midway point as well, and Hokit continued to walk forward. Wild punches from Hokit found a home with increasing regularity on the Frenchman, whose face bore a small smear of blood from his nose. They appeared to be getting to him.

Tired as he appeared, Gane fared better at stuffing takedowns, or at least not going down for long, early in the third. Instead, Hokit switched to clinch work and dirty boxing to find success on offense. He force-fed flips of the bird to cap off the frame, a staple of his public persona. Gane was not without his own damage dealt in the frame, however.

Gane, finding a second wind but clearly not up on the scorecards, mixed in some big knees early in the fourth, but little deterred Hokit from coming forward on this night. Clinch work once again was Hokit’s bread and butter, though Gane was more active in establishing enough high-impact offense to perhaps top Hokit’s output.

The final round began as most had before, with a Hokit takedown attempt. Gane defended, and a phone-booth boxing match ensued. The technique of Gane helped him find more accurate lands early on than the more wild ex-football player. But the fifth round was as competitive as the last two, and the offense hardly relented before the final horn before awaiting the official decision.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Comedian Bill Maher issued a preemptive warning to Democrats after their sweeping midterm election wins, urging the party not to mistake its victories for a mandate to revive “bad ideas” that could drive voters back to the GOP.

“Now that Democrats won the election, let’s not get high on our own supply like the last crowd did and interpret the W as a sign to go back to bad ideas,” he said during Friday’s episode of “Real Time.”

The liberal comedian pointed to “defund the police” and a refusal to enforce shoplifting laws, arguing that such approaches hurt the people progressives claim to help.

Maher also mocked progressives he described as the “lawn sign people,” accusing them of using yard signs touting equality, science and kindness to advertise their moral superiority.

“It’s all well and good to declare yourself the morally enlightened ones, but when your policy ideas are based on how good they make you feel and not on how much good they actually do, that’s when people lurch to the other even worse extreme,” he said.

Criticizing policies in Democratic-led cities, Maher asked, “Who benefited when you didn’t enforce the laws against shoplifting? Who benefits when you give a homeless schizophrenic clean needles instead of forcing him into treatment?”

Maher also criticized what he characterized as white liberals’ approach to racial issues, joking, “I talked to every black person in America, and it turns out they kind of don’t give a s—. Yeah. Turns out they’re not waking up every day saying, ‘What can I do today to make sure white people feel better about themselves?’”

Tim Graham, the executive editor of the Media Research Center’s NewsBusters blog, told Fox News Digital, “None of the elitist media are anywhere near the kind of tough-love advice counselor for Democrats, and especially not in public. If they wanted to tell Democrats that their gooey intentions aren’t equivalent to outcomes, they’d do it off the record.”

Christian Toto, the editor of Hollywood in Toto, told Fox News Digital, “Bill Maher is the most refreshing, unexpected pundit on late-night TV. He calls balls and strikes while simultaneously copping to his liberal bona fides.”

Toto added that Maher is “a pariah of sorts within his industry” and predicted that the “modern left will happily ignore his wisdom, likely at their political peril.”

Jason Mudd, CEO of Axia Public Relations, told Fox News Digital, “If the Democratic Party were my client, I’d advise them to remember this win was more about Trump than about the party.

“They should lean moderate to win over more voters. I’d also have trusted advisors with an objective or contrarian view screen each message before it goes public.”

Maher also criticized conservatives, arguing that Democrats won across several states in the midterms because voters have a history of shifting from one political extreme to another.

He first rejected what he characterized as Democratic moral superiority, then criticized what he described as Republicans’ embrace of “cruelty.”

“Republicans lost this election because no one wanted the pendulum to swing all the way to full a–hole, to cruelty,” he said.

“Yes, liberal virtue signaling had become tiresome, but did we have to go to vice signaling?”

Maher pointed to fatal shootings during immigration enforcement, cuts to the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) and other incidents as examples of what he believed caused the political pendulum to swing back to the left.

“This is how you lose even Texas,” he insisted, referring to wins for Democrats James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa in the longtime red stronghold.

“Everything is a reaction to what went before,” he added later.

Maher made the comments as Republicans review their midterm losses and reassess the party’s strategy ahead of the 2028 elections.

Republican candidates were upset in a handful of red and purple states, including South Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Mississippi and Georgia earlier this month, leading to Democratic majorities in both houses of Congress.
